guarantees.claim: key_length is assigned the value of key_length_supplied if it matches a supported key length (Key_128, Key_256, Key_384, Key_512, Key_1024); for any other value, key_length is assigned Key_None.

assumptions.claim: Downstream control logic must detect when key_length equals Key_None (due to an unsupported key_length_supplied) and prevent the HMAC core from starting operation, also signaling an error to software.
assumptions.cond: when key_length_supplied is an unsupported value and a subsequent HMAC start is triggered
assumptions.risk: HMAC may be activated with an unsupported key length, potentially leading to cryptographic weakness, data corruption, or side-channel leakage.

uncertain_points.claim: The comment asserts that starting HMAC with a key length mapped to Key_None is blocked and an error is signaled to software, but this chunk only performs the mapping. The existence and correctness of the downstream blocking/error logic must be verified elsewhere.
uncertain_points.cond: when key_length_supplied is unsupported and an HMAC start trigger occurs
uncertain_points.risk: If the blocking logic is missing or flawed, an unsupported key length could be used, compromising the security of HMAC operations.
